Build prompt

Rebuild this animation 1:1: Outlook's multi-select onboarding demo - a looped tutorial where email-row avatars shrink, morph into red checkmarks with a springy overshoot bounce, and rows get checked off one by one.

## Integration
Integration: stack-agnostic spec - springs given as stiffness/damping, timed motions as duration + curve; map every value to your framework and animation library of choice.

## Scene
Bottom-sheet style card in a phone frame: title "Multi-select with a tap", subtitle "Just tap the profile picture in an email to select multiple messages", a list of 3-4 email rows (colored circular avatar + gray placeholder text bars), and a red "Got It" button.

## Motion spec
Pattern: avatar-to-checkmark morph with spring overshoot, looped.
- Demo loop: a simulated tap lands on a row's avatar; the avatar circle scales down to ~0.7 and morphs into a red filled circle with a white checkmark (~250ms), then overshoot-bounces to 1.0 (spring ~300/18, ~180ms settle).
- Rows select sequentially, ~500ms apart, each with the same morph + bounce; a faint check-circle placeholder appears on unselected rows first.
- After 3-4 rows are checked, selections clear with a quick reverse morph (~200ms) and the loop restarts.
- Title, text bars, and Got It button stay static throughout.

## Calibration
- The bounce is the personality: overshoot ~1.15x scale on settle, one oscillation only.
- Sequential rhythm (500ms apart) reads as deliberate taps, not a bulk select.

## Reduced motion
Avatars swap to checkmarks without morph or bounce (150ms).

## Don't miss
- Only the avatar circle animates; the row text bars never move.
- The red check circle is the same size as the avatar it replaces - no jump in the row layout.
